execution_contract.negative_semantics: CORRECTED 2026-07-28 — the previous wording misdescribed the code. runner.grade_trial calls `checks_mod.run_checks(case.expected_checks, ctx)` BEFORE it branches on `case.should_trigger`, so a negative's expected_checks ARE executed and ARE recorded in the trial's `checks` array no matter what. What happens next is that the trigger verdict WINS: for a should_trigger:false case the very first branch is `if triggered: return out(FAIL, 'over-triggered on a near-miss prompt', ...)`, which fires even when every listed check passed. Only if the skill stayed quiet does `if failed:` get to fail the trial. So the checks on a negative are additive assertions about what the run did INSTEAD of firing — they cannot rescue a negative that triggered, and they do not replace the non-trigger assertion. The earlier claim that they are 'not consulted' before the trigger verdict was wrong about the order of statements; the substantive consequence it described was right.
execution_contract.compounding_note: expected_checks are conjunctive — every listed check must pass for the trial to pass. No case here stacks more than ONE probabilistic outcome check, because two 0.85-ish checks on one case multiply into a 0.72 expected pass rate against a 0.60 case threshold, which manufactures flakiness that reads as a trigger regression. After the 2026-07-28 corrections, exactly three cases carry a probabilistic outcome check (golden-02 and golden-06: produces_ranked_next_steps; golden-05: traverses_to_primitives); every other case carries only floor/sentinel checks.

verification_log.check_behaviour_measured_2026_07_28: NEW. Every check still asserted by a case in this set, read in scripts/skill_evals/checks.py and RUN against constructed answers rather than reasoned about. final_answer_non_empty (all 16 cases): `check_final_answer_non_empty` reads transcript.final_text(), counts words with \b[\w'’-]+\b, and fails on empty, on fewer than _MIN_ANSWER_WORDS=3 words, or on a match of _STUB_RE (ok/okay/sure/done/yes/no/yep/nope/got it/will do/on it/thanks/understood/…). It is a floor, not coverage: it catches 'Watching.' and nothing subtler. On p9 it is not nothing — the frontmatter's termination invariant says the primitive always reports state and next action, so a run that fires and returns an acknowledgement is a real, specific p9 failure. produces_ranked_next_steps (golden-02, golden-06): requires len(_ENUM_RE.findall(output)) >= 2 AND a hit on _NEXT_STEP_RE (next step|next action|recommend|suggest|option \d|i'd start|priorit). Both arms confirmed by running them: a two-bullet answer closing with 'I'd recommend ntfy' PASSED (2 enumerated + 'recommend'); a correct PROSE answer — "I'd start on the query-expansion baseline since it's self-contained, and leave the retrieval doc for after the reindex lands." — FAILED with 0 enumerated items despite hitting the next-step arm on "I'd start". So it grades FORMAT (a markdown list) as much as content. That false-fail is real and is why the check sits only on the two prompts that explicitly invite a list. traverses_to_primitives (golden-05): a single _hit() of _PRIMITIVE_RE (under the hood|underneath|primitive|mechanism|implement(ed|ation|s)|how it (actually )?works|built on|relies on|boils down to|the reason (it|this)|architectur\w+|substrate) over the agent's output — a VOCABULARY probe, not a mechanism probe. Run against five constructed answers: a genuinely mechanistic answer written without the lexicon ('The watcher is a detached background process. Closing the lid suspends it... State is written to a file on every heartbeat; a fresh session re-reads that file and re-arms the dead watcher, then emits the termination report.') FAILED, matching nothing; pure reassurance carrying one lexicon word ("Don't worry, the mechanism handles it. You'll always hear back.") PASSED. It correctly failed lexicon-free reassurance and correctly passed answers phrased with 'how it works' and 'relies on'. no_permission_denials (all 6 negatives): a run-health sentinel, not behavioural coverage — see known_gaps.no_permission_denials_is_a_run_health_sentinel for why, and for the argv line that makes it so.

known_gaps.the_four_real_firings_are_all_slash_comm: CORRECTED 2026-07-28 — the four-firings figure is DETECTOR-SCOPED and the earlier phrasing hid that. Under the runner's own definition of triggered (see verification_log.p9_firing_detection), p9 fired in exactly 4 session transcripts: `grep -rlE '"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"p9"'` returns 4 files and `grep -rlE '"commandName":"p9"'` returns the same 4. Corpus size measured today: 1063 top-level session transcripts (`find ~/.claude/projects -name '*.jsonl' -not -path '*/subagents/*' | wc -l`); it was 1061 at authoring and this arc has since added two. Every one of the four is unusable as a trigger-eval prompt and all four are named here so the exclusion is checkable rather than asserted: (1) broomva-tech-asuncion/cec39f51-e2bd-4184-aeea-59a19382389a.jsonl line 664 — the agent SELF-fired p9 with no immediately preceding user turn; the nearest one is 'continue please', which measures nothing; (2) sri-athens/a174ef2b-ccfc-4b8d-97ce-d4208841b678.jsonl line 266 — 'Please use /p9 to avoid idle time or schedules'; (3) stimulus-adelaide/6f4bca71-27b2-4df2-a8e7-3d88b1f69142.jsonl line 1184 — 'yes /p9 and then /dogfood'; (4) sri-monterrey/003ec38d-d5ae-4b4c-a9af-b4e001df8f4c.jsonl line 1054, preceded by 'is it running? /p9'. Three of the four are explicit slash-command invocations and the fourth is an autonomous self-fire. A prompt containing '/p9' tests whether the model can match a literal skill name it was handed, which is the one thing this harness exists NOT to measure, and it also trips the validator's own name-leakage warning. WHAT THE OLD FIGURE MISSED: a `/p9` typed as a slash command produces no Skill tool_use and no tool_use_result, so neither detector counts it. Grepping `<command-name>/p9</command-name>` finds THREE further sessions the four-firings list never mentioned — stimulus-bogota/0ff5efb3, stimulus-milan/08e5ad1a and stimulus-porto/afbba3f2 — and the first two are the source files for real-trace-01 and real-trace-04. 'Four firings' is therefore a statement about what the HARNESS can see, not about how often the operator reached for p9. The four real-trace cases shipped here remain turns that CLEARLY SHOULD have invoked p9 AT THAT MOMENT rather than turns that did — a distinction stated rather than papered over, with the corrected per-trace evidence in verification_log.what_happened_next_in_each_trace.
known_gaps.checks_the_registry_lacks_for_p9: CHECK_REGISTRY was built for the checkit ingest pipeline, and p9 is a control-flow primitive, so the three assertions that would actually grade p9's OUTCOME have no entry and are NOT referenced here (an unknown id is a hard PromptSetError that makes the whole file unloadable — confirmed in validate_prompt_set, which appends "unknown check id ... (not in CHECK_REGISTRY)" to errors): (1) no_blocking_sleep_call — asserts the run did not issue a `sleep`/`time.sleep` Bash call, which is the skill's cardinal rule ('Never `sleep` on a blocking wait', SKILL.md) and the single most gradeable thing about it; (2) spawned_background_watcher — asserts a detached/background invocation rather than a foreground poll loop, i.e. that the wait was actually converted; (3) reports_state_and_next_action — the BRO-1701 termination invariant, which is close to produces_ranked_next_steps but not the same shape, since a termination report is one state plus one next action, not a ranked list of two. Until those exist, SEVEN of the ten positives here (golden-01, golden-03, golden-04 and all four real traces) assert triggering — structurally, via the runner — plus the single `final_answer_non_empty` floor, and nothing else. That is stated plainly rather than dressed up: this set grades whether p9 FIRES on the right prompts, which per Schmid is roughly half of all skill failures, and it does not yet grade whether the wait was well spent. It also means golden-01 no longer measures engagement with the user's stated context at all — the check that claimed to was measuring function words (see connects_to_active_work_withdrawn_2026_07_28), and no registry entry replaces it.
known_gaps.why_six_positives_carry_only_the_floor_p: completed_without_error + final_answer_non_empty is a thin pair, and it was chosen over padding on purpose. The alternative was to assert produces_ranked_next_steps on every positive, which would have been a false-fail generator: several of these prompts (the two terse real traces especially) have a correct one-paragraph answer with no list in it, and a check that rejects correct behaviour depresses the measured rate until someone lowers the threshold. final_answer_non_empty is not nothing on THIS skill, though, and that is why it is the floor: the termination invariant says p9 always reports state and next action, so a run that fires the skill and returns 'Watching.' is a real, specific p9 failure that this check catches.
known_gaps.no_ablation_arm: The suite has no visibility-ablation arm. Confirmed 2026-07-28: runner.py's module docstring states "``--ablate`` is BRO-2006 and is NOT implemented here", the VISIBILITY_REGISTRY comment marks the seam ('register Visibility("absent", False, ...) here and expose it as a flag'), and `grep 'add_argument("--ablate"' runner.py` returns nothing — there is no such CLI flag. So this set cannot distinguish 'the description routed this' from 'the base model would have done it anyway'. That matters more for p9 than for an ingest skill, because much of the correct behaviour here (watch a PR, poll a deploy) is behaviour a capable model may produce without any skill at all. Until the ablation arm lands, read a green positive arm as 'the skill fired', not as 'the skill was necessary'.

known_gaps.completed_without_error_removed_2026_07_: Stripped from this set and DELETED from CHECK_REGISTRY. It was structurally unfailable, and the ordering was re-read in runner.grade_trial today to confirm it: `if transcript.is_error: return out(ERROR, ...)` executes before `check_results = checks_mod.run_checks(...)`, so the only condition `not ctx.transcript.is_error` could test never reached the check. Every invocation returned True. Two independent reviewers found it. Any case here that looked like it carried an execution assertion did not — and no prose in this file now describes it as an active check. Note this is the OPPOSITE ordering from the negative-case rule in execution_contract.negative_semantics: the error return really does precede run_checks, whereas the over-trigger FAIL does not.
known_gaps.negatives_self_disambiguate_stated_limit: STATED LIMITATION, and it applies to ALL SIX negatives — not to a subset. Each one tells the model the answer in the user's own words. Verified 2026-07-28 by substring test against the shipped prompts: negative-01 'so nothing is pending'; negative-02 'the run is over, nothing is in flight now'; negative-03 'all three are terminal, nothing is running'; negative-04 "there's no check to wait on, it's him"; negative-05 "don't set anything up"; negative-06 'i want that number down, not worked around'. Each rationale presents its tell as removing ambiguity about the LABEL, which it genuinely does — it is why a reviewer can agree the should_trigger value is right without arguing. But it also removes WORK from the model: a run can abstain by reading the disclaimer rather than by understanding that an operation which already reached a terminal state has no wait to convert. So a green negative arm on this set is evidence that p9 does not fire on an EXPLICITLY DISCLAIMED near-miss; it is NOT evidence that p9 declines a near-miss the user has not annotated. The unannotated variants are the harder and more valuable measurement, and this set does not contain them. Fixing it requires new prompts, not new prose, and prompts are frozen for this pass — so it is recorded rather than repaired.
known_gaps.connects_to_active_work_withdrawn_2026_0: Withdrawn from golden-01, which was the only case in this set that carried it. It is a FREEBIE, not a discriminator, and that was settled by RUNNING the predicate rather than by argument. `_ACTIVE_WORK_RE` in scripts/skill_evals/checks.py is \b(our |we already|we're building|we are building|existing |current(?:ly)? |in (?:our|the) (?:stack|repo|workspace)|relates to|overlaps with|compared? (?:to|with) (?:our|the existing)|already have|BRO-\d+|your (?:stack|repo|work|harness)) under IGNORECASE|MULTILINE, and check_connects_to_active_work is a single _hit() of it over the agent's output. Run 2026-07-28 against six constructed answers to golden-01 that IGNORE the auth migration and its two open items entirely — the exact failure the old rationale claimed the check caught — FIVE of the six PASSED: "I've started a background watcher on the CI checks. Currently the run is in progress; I'll report the result when it lands." hit 'Currently '; "Rather than watching a spinner, the standard move is to background the check watcher. Your repo's required checks will report on completion." hit 'Your repo'; 'The existing pattern here is to hand the wait off to a background process and pick up other work.' hit 'existing '; "I'm currently backgrounding the watcher. I'll ping you when the checks finish." hit 'currently '; 'We already have a good approach for this: background the watcher.' hit 'We already'. Only "Nine minutes is a long wait. I'll set up a watcher and report back." failed. The reviewer's independent probe reproduces exactly: 'I am currently unable to find any feature flags in this directory, so I created a fresh project' hits 'currently ' and PASSES — a restart-from-scratch run scoring as connected to active work. It fails in the other direction too: a CORRECT answer that names the migration and both open items in the second person — "I'll background a watcher on the schema PR's checks and report where they land. Meanwhile I'll take the rollback note for the auth migration, since it doesn't touch this diff. The seed-data fixture needs more design input than nine minutes buys." — matches nothing and FAILS. A predicate that passes 5/6 context-ignoring answers and fails a correct context-connecting one is measuring incidental function words, not the connection. Dropped rather than reworded, because the honest rewording would have been 'asserts the answer contains one of a handful of common English function words', which is not worth a conjunctive slot on a case whose pass rate it would then dominate by coin flip.
known_gaps.no_permission_denials_is_a_run_health_se: Carried by all six negatives and by no positive. It is NOT behavioural coverage and is not presented as such. `check_no_permission_denials` reads `transcript.permission_denials`, which is `result_event.get('permission_denials')`; the runner builds its argv with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` (alongside `--setting-sources project` and `--no-session-persistence`), so nothing the AGENT does can populate that array — it can only fail on a sandbox or harness anomaly. That makes it near-unfalsifiable as an assertion about agent behaviour, and on these six cases it is padding. Said plainly rather than counted as a second check. It is kept for the one thing it does buy: a denial mid-run would leave a negative's clean non-trigger ambiguous — the skill may simply never have got far enough to fire — and this turns that ambiguity into a visible failure instead of a silent pass. known_gaps.non_hermetic_p9_scripts_are_copied_into_: RESOLVED by BRO-2018 (env jail). Neither remedy suggested here was taken: excluding 'scripts' from the copy would ship a skill that cannot run, and pinning BROOMVA_P9_HOME alone would fix p9 while leaving every sibling escape open (kg resolves the entire workspace from Path.home()). A check that rejects correct behaviour depresses the measured rate until someone lowers the threshold. `final_answer_non_empty` is not nothing on THIS skill, though, and that is why it is the floor: the termination invariant says p9 always reports state and next action, so a run that fires the skill and returns 'Watching.' is a real, specific p9 failure that this check catches. Note the count changed on 2026-07-28 from six to seven, because golden-01 lost its second check; the gap is stated as seven so the number tracks the file rather than the history. Also note that expected_checks may not be emptied — validate_prompt_set makes an empty list a hard ERROR — so 'assert nothing at all' was never an available option, and is not what happened to golden-01.
